lines.en: After making my way back to the campground, I find Maki sitting beside a lake that looks more like a large puddle in a rare moment of somewhat quiet contemplation for her.
And the only reason it’s somewhat and not genuinely quiet contemplation is the fact that I can hear Haruka chatting up Sara and Ami inside of their tent not that far from here.

But, not wanting to intrude (And also being given the rare opportunity to hang out with Maki in an area where she can not immediately reach for a plastic horse penis), I can’t help but indulge and make my way over.
She notices me immediately and gazes back with eyes that scream both “I have no idea what I’m doing” and “I’m glad you came over because I was bored as hell.”
: Hey! I’m glad you came over because I was bored as hell. And also, I have no idea what I’m doing.
Cool. I guess I know her better than I thought.
: Why bother fishing if you have no idea what you’re doing?

: Thought I’d try learning. But apparently, this isn’t something you can just sit down and do. But hey, not much else is going on right now. So maybe this will bring me closer to nature or something like that.
: I didn’t take you as the type of woman who’d want to be closer to nature in any capacity.
: And I didn’t take you as the type of man who’d go out of his way to bring his niece camping just because he thought it might make her happy.
: But I’m glad that you are.
: It’ll make packing up all of our gear a lot easier tomorrow morning.
: Is there an extra chair I could set up next to you?
: Ooooh, is it bondage time?
: You know damn well that the word is “bonding.”
: I have no idea what you’re talking about. But yes, there are a few extra chairs in my trunk. You just might have to move a few things out of the way first. Only a handful of them bite, though.
: There are toys for all sorts of people nowadays, aren’t there?
: They’re the backbone keeping society propped up and I refuse to believe otherwise.
: You know, I can’t say I disagree. But I feel like your thoughts on this matter are a lot more passionate than mine, so I’m just going to dig through your trunk now.
: Jeez, Akira. At least lube yourself up first. That’s a sensitive spot and I’m a fragile young woman.
I ignore Maki’s somewhat flirtatious prodding for what I imagine is the millionth time in my life as I make my way over to her car.
I prop the chair up beside her and sink down into it, digging my heels into the grass to prevent it from slipping away and sending me face first into the water and then subsequently her hook.
She looks at me again and pauses for a moment, but I can’t discern what her gaze is saying this time. So I just look back at her. And I wonder if she’s trying to figure out what my eyes are saying.

I get compliments on them a lot, but I’ve never understood why. And, more often than not, it leads me to believe that the words themselves are empty and only exist to curry favor with a potential mate.
There’s none of that here, though. We’re just two confused adults who happen to exist at the same time, fighting our own battles and pretending to be stronger than we actually are.
It’s the illusion that matters, after all. Because things are only real once you can see them. And if you can never see pain, you can trick yourself into believing it doesn’t exist.
I know why Maki’s fishing.
And I can promise you that nature has nothing to do with it.
: You know...you’re a good guy, Akira.
You’re only saying that because you still don’t know I’m screwing your daughter.
i’m glad you said it because i was going to if you didn’t.
Why not make me say it out loud then? That’s a thing you can do, isn’t it?
beep boop bop. too far out of service area. waiting for more bars. try back later.
So I can get away from you if I just stay out here?
maybe. but then you’d run out of cumsluts and drown yourself in the river and i don’t know how to swim.
: Are you always this quiet after getting a compliment? Or are you still just trying to figure out how to respond?
: Sorry. Just...thinking.
: I get it. That’s kind of why I’m out here trying new things in the first place.
: Masahiro liked fishing. He’d take Makoto out with him from time to time.
: Said it was his way of calming down. But he was always pretty mild-mannered to begin with.
: Guess you never really know what’s going through someone’s head, though. Like, for all I know, maybe he was miserable? Maybe he only needed to “calm down” because I was stressing him out?
: I doubt that was it. You might be weird, but you don’t seem like a stressful partner.
: You’re probably right. Or at least that’s what I’ll keep telling myself since it’s not like I can really ask anymore.
: But even if he’s gone now, I still feel like I can connect with him if I do things like this. So I guess it’s less about being “one with nature” and more about being “one with dead husband.”
: That was actually really sweet up until the end.
: Yeah, that made me sound kind of like a necrophiliac, didn’t it?
: That’s most assuredly not where my mind went, but it’s a very Maki way of interpreting it, so I guess I’m not surprised.
: Do you think you’d ever bone a zombie if you were given the chance?
: Is that really what we’re going to talk about? I was expecting more of a serious conversation after the way this talk started.
: Can we not have a serious conversation about the ethics of having sex with a dead body?
: I take it that means you would?
: I’m not sure, actually. Like, can zombies even get boners? Is it just always hard because of the rigor mortis?
: Maki, are you doing okay? Because I can leave you alone if you’re only doing this right now to connect with your husband. I wasn’t trying to interrupt that.

: Thank you for that...but I’m fine. I’ll probably just stick to fishing in porn games and connect with Masahiro in other ways. Like eating his favorite foods or...recommending elderly porn to my customers.
: This is not a thing I ever needed to know or learn, so thanks for that.

: Dead men tell no tales, so their widows must sing their glories instead. Even if their glories involve fishing and watching grandma take a massive dong up her cooter like she’s back in her twenties again.
: You miss him, don’t you?
: Yeah.
: But that’s not something I expect to ever go away. I mean...how can it?
: Falling in love is, like...it’s something that changes a person. It’s not a thing you can just fall out of once one side isn’t there anymore.
: That’s okay, though. I want to keep those feelings because I really did love that mild-mannered elder fucker. And- you know what, Akira? If he was a zombie, I’d still let him hit it.
: I’m putting a lot of faith in rigor mortis right now though and I hope you know that.
: Akira?...
: Do you have, like...advice?
: For...for parenting, you mean? I thought that’s why Sara-
: For moving on after losing someone you love.
: I know we haven’t really, like...talked ever since I started coming back to the shop. But that’s kind of what caused this whole shitty situation in the first place.
: And seeing you out here doing things like fishing just because your husband used to do it makes me want to try and kind of...take matters into my own hands as well.
: Like, Ami’s not the only person who I hope this trip helps out. But I’m so torn between wanting to feel better and thinking I don’t deserve to that I have no way of knowing what to actually do.
: All I know is that everything I see reminds me of someone I can’t let go of. And I was wondering if you had any, like...advice on what I should be latching onto or not.
: Do the others know?
: Not yet. And I didn’t even plan on telling you until a minute ago. I just can’t help but admire how...resilient you are.
: There’s nothing I can say that will make you feel any better.
: Yeah...I figured as much.

: It sucks, I know. And, just like with Makoto, I wish there was something I can do. But if there’s anything I’ve unfortunately learned lately, it’s that moving past something like this entirely comes down to you.
: No matter what you tell me, I’ll never understand the way you saw the person you’re referring to. Just like how you’ll never understand what I had with Masahiro.

: All we can do is relate to one another and share in each other’s experience and...maybe that helps a little. But it pales in comparison to the pain that returns when all those precious memories start flooding in.
: It’s going to hurt for the rest of your life.
: But there are other things that can keep you grounded.
: That’s probably why I’m putting so much of myself into Ami right now.
: That is illegal in several ways, good sir.
: Maki, come on.
: On or in? Because pulling out of Ami makes things a little more socially acceptable, but still. Not a smart move, man.
: Just...forget I even said anything.
: I’m just trying to lighten the mood, Akira. I know you and Ami don’t have that kind of relationship.
Yeah. It’s much worse than you could probably imagine.

: I understand exactly what you mean when you say you’re putting all of yourself into Ami because that’s exactly what I’m doing with Makoto. Just...in a way that’s very hands-off and doesn’t annoy her.
: You think your happiness will come from her, right? So you want her to feel better because that will make you feel like you’re doing something right.
: I guess you grasp the situation a lot better than you let on.
: Because it’s the same situation, Akira. We’re parents. Both of us. Not just me.
: I don’t deserve to be called a parent.
: And I do?! I didn’t take up the mantle of “Mom” until my husband passed away. That’s why Makoto has such a hard time even seeing me as a proper mother.
: And...I have no clue who the person you’re talking about is, but maybe that’ll serve as yours and Ami’s prompt for sneaking a bit of normalcy back into your lives.
: I’m just...not sure if I can do it, Maki.
: Doubting yourself is just part of the process, Akira. No one’s good at this right away. It’s scary having someone else’s life in your hands. Especially when that person is smart.
: And yeah, Ami might not be Makoto-smart. But I’ve heard about what happened to her parents and I can almost assure you that sort of event would make her at least emotionally mature.
: Yeah...I’m not so sure about that.
: That’s not really a thing we ever talk about in our house.
: Mm...so that’s the way it is.
: Sorry. I didn’t know.

: There’s nothing to apologize for. I just have to figure out a way to make this work on my own. Learning coping techniques from someone else who experienced something similar would have been way too easy.
: Like I said, though...there are things out there that can keep you grounded. And Ami is the biggest one of all.
: Yeah...you’re right.
: I need to get my shit together for her sake.
: I can’t be hurting right now as all that will do is make things even harder for her.
: Exactly...
: But that doesn’t mean it’s okay to just give up on yourself either, okay?

: Do you understand what I’m saying here? It’s fine to prioritize her. You should be prioritizing her. But you’re a human as well, Akira. And being upset is, like...the most human thing I can even think of.
: Yeah, I hear you.
: So you agree that you’ll try and take care of yourself when you really need to?
: I’ll see what I can do.
: Akira-
: I’ll talk to you later, Maki.
: Hah...
: Okay.
: I’ll be here if you need me.
I make my way back into a space between the trees...
And I think of other ways to kill the time.
Maki’s affection has increased to [maki_love]!
Now what?
: But...
: You know...I wouldn’t really mind being another one...
: If Ami’s not enough, I mean.
: Which isn’t me saying that I think I should be even close to as important in your life as she is, just that I...well...you know...
: Like...you and me are...I kind of...well, like...uhh...how should I put this?
: I don’t know, Maki. How should you put it?
: Well, it’s...it’s kind of, like...like, it’s no secret that I see you a little differently than the rest of my friends.
: And...while it’s not the same way I see Masahiro or...saw Masahiro...it doesn’t mean you aren’t, like...it doesn’t mean that, uhh...
: It doesn’t mean that you...aren’t something I...don’t want to protect.
: That...was too many negatives in one sentence. I need a second to parse-
: It means you can lean on me because I like you. Okay? There. I said it.
: You didn’t have to say it, Maki. I already knew that.
: Then you should have cut me off before I started stammering like that! I’m not good at sounding cute and this is what happens when I try!
: I mean, ignoring how your inability to be cute is what makes you cute, you shouldn’t feel pressured to say or do things like that.
: I know you’ll be there if I need you. And just talking to you today has already helped a lot.
: Hell, this whole trip has helped a lot and we’ve still got almost a full day ahead of us. So thanks for that. And thanks for giving me the opportunity to...try and make things better.
: I can’t promise to lean more on you in the future as...I’m not really in a position now to promise anyone anything.
: But you’re important to me as well. And I’m flattered you’d even consider accepting me after falling so hard for someone who fit you so much better.
: And I’m flattered you’d consider accepting me when I’ve had so many penises and penis-shaped objects inside of me that most would consider it a major turn off.
: And now the moment is ruined.
: Ruined? Or better?
: Ruined, Maki. Now there’s no way I can have a nice, emotional send off.
: You can’t have a send off at all if I leave first!
: Maki-
: Bye!
Maki leaps out of her chair and sprints into the woods, but I’m able to catch a glimpse of how red her face is just before she vanishes into the trees.
And I think for a moment about why she’d look that way for me.
I think about how my existence has subtly conned her into believing she could ever squeeze anything out of me that isn’t just semen — and I feel both shameful and regretful as a result of this.
I’m ashamed because I doubt I could ever love her.
But I’m regretful to have ever loved at all.
For life would be so much easier if she were the one I wanted the most.
Doubting that Maki will be returning any time soon, I head back to a place between the trees and think of what else to do before the sun sets.
Maki’s affection has increased to [maki_love]!
What now?
